newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine sugar millers have large unsold stocks.
newsitem.headline: Philippine sugar millers have large unsold stocks.

text.p: Philippine sugar millers have unsold stocks of 100,000 tonnes in warehouses, the Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa told reporters on Wednesday.
Gamboa said the SRA would consult sugar producers on what might be the best time to release the stocks in the market.
"We don't want to dampen prices," he said.
Gamboa said of the unsold stocks of 100,000 tonnes, 27,000 tonnes belonged to Victorias Milling Co, which last week reported problems repaying debts of 4.423 billion pesos ($168 million).
In a statement issued at the news conference, the SRA said Victorias carrying cost of the unsold sugar had mounted to at least 100 million pesos in the past 10 months.
The statement said the SRA was taking steps to protect the interests of the sugar industry.
"There cannot be a run and neither shall there be high speculation and manipulation adverse to consumers and users," it said.
But the Victorias stocks had to be released, the SRA said.
Factors it mentioned that merit the "immediate release" of the stocks included the high carrying cost and the fact that the stocks had already been stored for 10 months.
It said the stocks had come from valid imports and noted the SRA has no power over imported sugar.
On Tuesday, a committee formed by Victorias 32 creditors sought a faster financial audit of the company so they could recommend a recovery plan.
